blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: HCF (Highest Common Factor) and LCM (Lowest Common Multiple) are foundational concepts for numeric operations.
The two standard techniques for evaluating HCF and LCM are the Prime Factorisation Method and the Division Method.
For any two positive numbers, the product of the numbers equals the product of their HCF and LCM.
HCF of fractions is given by the HCF of Numerators divided by the LCM of Denominators.
LCM of fractions is given by the LCM of Numerators divided by the HCF of Denominators.
HCF of two or more numbers is the greatest number that divides each of them exactly.

LCM of two or more numbers is the smallest number which is exactly divisible by each of them.

In SSC examination, questions from LCM & HCF are:

• Direct

• Formula-based

• Application-oriented (word problems)

blocks.content:
Steps:

1. Resolve each number into prime factors.

2. For HCF, take common prime factors with the lowest power.

3. For LCM, take all prime factors with the highest power.

Steps:

1. Divide the numbers by the smallest possible prime number.

2. Continue dividing till no further division is possible.

3. Product of the divisors gives the HCF.

4. Product of the divisors and remaining numbers gives the LCM.

items:
For two numbers:

HCF × LCM = Product of the two numbers

blocks.content:
Example:

1)If HCF = 6 and LCM = 180, and one number is 30, find the other.



6 × 180 = 30 × x

x = 36

Numbers are 30 and 36.

items:
HCF of fractions:

HCF = (HCF of numerators) / (LCM of denominators)

LCM of fractions:

LCM = (LCM of numerators) / (HCF of denominators)

rows: The largest number that divides all given numbers without leaving a remainder.
The smallest number that is a multiple of all given numbers.
HCF of Numerators / LCM of Denominators
LCM of Numerators / HCF of Denominators

blocks.content:
Example 1:

Two numbers have HCF = 12 and LCM = 180. If one number is 36, find the other.

Solution:

12 × 180 = 36 × x

x = 60

Example 2:

A bell rings every 6 minutes and another every 8 minutes. After how much time will they ring together?

Solution:

LCM of 6 and 8 = 24 minutes

• HCF of two co-prime numbers is 1.

• LCM of two co-prime numbers is their product.

• HCF always divides LCM.

• LCM is always greater than or equal to the greatest number.

items: The formula 'Product of two numbers = HCF × LCM' holds true ONLY for two numbers, not for three or more numbers.
Always convert fractions into their simplest form before computing their HCF or LCM.
In word problems, questions asking for 'maximum length/capacity' require HCF, while questions on 'minimum time/simultaneous events' (e.g., bells ringing together) require LCM.

blocks.content:
Q1. Find the HCF of 18 and 42.

A. 6 B. 12 C. 18 D. 21



Q2. Find the LCM of 12, 15 and 20.

A. 60 B. 120 C. 180 D. 240



Q3. The HCF and LCM of two numbers are 8 and 96. If one number is 24, find the other.

A. 32 B. 36 C. 48 D. 64
